rationale: The candidate reads consistently across the four views as one dominant U-shaped/bridged mass with a clear internal court and a legible ground void toward the verified access edge. It is not a coherent form in only one view; the plan, oblique, and opposing views agree on the same spatial rule, and there is no obvious cross-view collision. The parcel response appears coherent: the mass occupies the boundary as a perimeter figure rather than merely filling a box. The blue access edge is answered by a visible open seam/court rather than a sealed frontage, which aligns well with the neighborhood-living brief. The silhouette is somewhat blocky and not especially sectional, but the court/bridge condition keeps it from feeling arbitrary. It resonates most with the similar references through courtyard-driven neighborhood massing and bridge-like upper connection, though it is simpler and more rectilinear.

reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Three-part massing with a central void and an upper connector creates a legible public threshold while keeping the ground edge active.

reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Terraced/campus-like composition with a shared courtyard can scale to neighborhood living when the ground plane stays porous.
